name: highlight
description: Inline emphasis for the words a headline wants read first: accent-gradient text, a highlighter marker, a drawn underline, or a shimmer. Every effect is a background under or clipped to real text — selectable, searchable, announced once — and each can play its motion (pan, draw-in) from tokens. Pure CSS; restores plain text under forced colours.

animate.description: Play the variant's motion: the gradient pans back and forth, the marker and the underline are drawn in once from the start of the line. Shimmer always moves and ignores this.

--highlight-color.description: Ink of the marker and the underline (custom property). Pass a colour token.

--highlight-gradient.default: var(--gradient-accent), else the accent → info gradient
--highlight-gradient.description: The gradient clipped to the text (custom property). Defaults to the theme's --gradient-accent where the theme states one.

--highlight-delay.description: With data-animate on marker and underline: time before the stroke is drawn (custom property).

a11y.notes: Purely visual: a highlight is a span with no role, and the text inside is the only text there is. Gradient and shimmer set the fill transparent and paint the glyphs with a background, so their contrast is the gradient's contrast against the page — keep both gradient stops at 4.5:1 against the surface, or use the highlight on large text only. Marker and underline leave the text colour alone. Forced colours remove the effect and restore the system text colour.

notes: A few words, not a sentence: a highlight works because the rest of the line is plain.

Inside a hero headline it sits directly in the heading:

Ship your interface, not your design system

.
The gradient variant picks up a theme's signature gradient automatically — themes that define --gradient-accent (aurora) re-colour every gradient highlight on the page.
